summary: Philippe Stern (1895–1979) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held positions at the Musée Guimet (1927–1965), the Musée de la parole et du geste (around 1928), and the École du Louvre (1929–1965).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned his PhD from McGill University, supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori alongside several other teachers.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (1811–1894) studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1838, specializing in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, the University of Paris, and the Collège de France.
Phillip Emmanual Bloom works in Sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University under the supervision of Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996), Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), and President of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004).
Phra Khantipalo (1932–2021) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Chien Ming Chen and served as abbot at Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978.
Phra Maha Singhathon Narasabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the doctoral supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Phra Medhidhammaporn (born 1955) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis in 1985 at the University of Delhi under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. As of 2012, he served as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Phramaha Hansa Dhammahaso is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a post at the Nibbana Meditation Centre and served as Director at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University in 2017.
Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied under Luang Por Dhammajayo and earned a PhD from the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle.

Phuntsok Tashi (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (BA) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (MA), and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff (born 1947), an Indologist and scholar of Buddhism and religion, earned degrees from Radcliffe College and Harvard University. She served as Professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) before becoming Lex Hixon Professor Emeritus at Yale University in 2004.

Pierre Bourdieu (1930–2002) was a philosopher who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University, the EHESS, and the Collège de France (1981–2001).
Pierre Chantraine (1899–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between 1920 and 1927. He later held a post at the University of Paris from around 1937 to 1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry (1963–1967), the Chair of Sanskrit at EPHE (1967–2004), and positions at EHESS, Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and Société Asiatique.
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University by 1991 and was attested as a research fellow there in 1996.

Pieter Hendrik Pott (1918–1989) was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology. He served as curator at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

Pietro Merlo (1850–1888) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. From 1877, he taught at the University of Pavia, becoming an ordinary professor in 1885.
